bio_html:
Dr David Gunn is a Brisbane based ophthalmologist specialising in medical and surgical diseases of the cornea, complex cataract surgery and laser and refractive eye surgery.

He was educated in Brisbane and graduated from The University of Queensland Bachelor of Science and Medicine programs awarded with First Class Honours. He completed his medical residency and ophthalmology training throughout Queensland and was awarded the prestigious K. G. Howsam gold medal for obtaining the highest results in the Australian and New Zealand final ophthalmology examinations.

Dr Gunn undertook fellowship training at the Royal Brisbane and Women’s Hospital followed by further subspecialty training in corneal, advanced cataract and refractive surgery at the renowned Bristol Eye Hospital.

Dr Gunn practices at the Queensland Eye Institute and holds a public appointment at the Mater Hospital Brisbane where he also offers intermediate surgery to uninsured patients.

He is active in eye disease research and publishes in local and international medical journals. He is involved in the training of surgical registrars, medical students and nurses and is an honorary faculty member of The University of Queensland.

An international voice for corneal surgery

Dr Gunn was awarded the Certificate in Laser and Refractive Surgery by the Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK) and is a founding Fellow of the World College of Refractive Surgery and Visual Sciences. He consults at the Queensland Eye Institute, 87 Ipswich Road, Woolloongabba, with all surgery performed at South Brisbane Day Hospital, and is a senior lecturer in the School of Medicine at the University of Queensland.

In May 2021 Dr Gunn performed Australia's first CAIRS keratoplasty at the Queensland Eye Institute, a minimally invasive corneal transplant technique for keratoconus using donor corneal tissue that has since become an established alternative to full corneal grafts. Together with Dr Brendan Cronin and Dr Rebecca Cox he co-authored the Brisbane Nomogram, the world's first standardised surgical planning framework for CAIRS, published in Clinical and Experimental Ophthalmology (2026). In 2025 he delivered the Ridley Lecture at the German Ophthalmology Congress, has presented at the European Society of Cataract and Refractive Surgeons congresses in Vienna and Barcelona, conducted CAIRS surgical wet labs at the Southern African Society of Cataract and Refractive Surgery congress in 2026, and regularly teaches the technique to visiting surgeons from Asia-Pacific, Europe and North America.

Dr Gunn believes advances in surgical planning should be shared freely. With Dr Cronin he co-developed CAIRSPlan.com, the world's first free online surgical planning tool for CAIRS.
treats: Micro-incision cataract surgery with premium intraocular lens implantation
CAIRS keratoplasty for keratoconus and corneal ectasia (Medicare item 42653)
Customised femtosecond laser CAIRS on the Ziemer Z8 platform
LASIK, TransPRK, PRK and CLEAR laser eye surgery
Therapeutic excimer laser (PTK) for corneal scarring, dystrophies, recurrent erosions and irregular astigmatism
Sutureless pterygium surgery with conjunctival autograft
Corneal transplant surgery including DALK, DSAEK and DMEK
